title: Trump details his 'final 30 days' strategy to get Republicans elected in the midterms
text:
“I’m going to take the final 30 days, maybe a little bit more than that, because it’s all about 35 races,” Trump said. “I’m going to go to every one of those 35 places, and weR…
, the president plans to hit the campaign trail and host several tele-rallies as part of his push to keep the House and Senate in Republican hands, he explained in remarks to GOP lawmakers and administration officials at a White House Rose Garden dinner.
“I’m going to take the final 30 days, maybe a little bit more than that, because it’s all about 35 races,” Trump said. “I’m going to go to every one of those 35 places, and we’re going to see if we can get everyone elected. ” President Donald Trump speaks during an End of Summer BBQ event with Republican lawmakers in the Rose Garden of the White House on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in Washington, DC.
He didn’t say which races he had in mind – there are 35 Senate seats up for grabs in November – but asked the lawmakers in attendance, including House Speaker Mike Johnson , to “give me some names where, I say, is either tied, or you’re winning by a little bit, or you’re losing by a little bit. ” “In some cases, you can be losing by a lot, and we’ll bring you over the line,” Trump added.
“But mostly, it’s if you’re close – and we’ll get, I think, we’ll get all those people elected. ” also teased a flurry of “tele-townhalls,” as many as 10-per-night, in the run-up to the midterms. Trump pledged to travel to Texas to campaign for Senate candidate Ken Paxton, before joking: “You might not like the way he dresses. ”Trump also plans to travel to Alaska and stump for GOP Sen.
Dan Sullivan. Trump specifically pledged to campaign in Alaska, for incumbent GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan, and in Texas, for Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is locked in a tight Senate race with Democrat James Talarico. Trump compared the potentially brutal schedule to the final 120 days of his 2024 presidential campaign, during which he claims he swore-off playing golf.
“Four months out I said, ‘OK, no days off. ’ If I didn’t make 4-5 speeches a day it was very bad. I just went around and really campaigned hard,” he recalled.
“For 4 months, there will be no pleasure. I’m not gonna go play golf. … All I’m gonna do is work, work, work, fight, fight, fight, win, win, win … and I did. ” President Donald Trump speaks during an End of Summer BBQ event with Republican lawmakers in the Rose Garden of the White House on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in Washington, DC.
